claims: FIRE stands for Financial Independence, Retire Early.
The FIRE movement involves savings often 50–75% of income.
The FIRE movement aims to retire decades earlier than the traditional age of 65.
The traditional age of retirement is 65.
FIRE followers accumulate ~25 times their annual expenses.
The FIRE number is typically 25x annual expenses.
The 4% rule suggests you can safely withdraw 4% of your portfolio in the first year of retirement.
The 4% rule suggests adjusting the withdrawal for inflation thereafter.
Proponents of the FIRE movement are often millennials.
Proponents of the FIRE movement save 50% to 70%+ of their income.
Lean FIRE involves extreme frugality to retire as soon as possible.
Fat FIRE involves retiring early with a higher, more comfortable budget.
Barista FIRE involves partial retirement, working part-time for benefits/income.
Coast FIRE involves saving aggressively early, then allowing investments to grow, requiring only part-time work to cover expenses.
The FIRE number is calculated by multiplying annual expenses by 25.
